title: What counts as a hit, and what a No Bird is
summary: In Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting a target is a hit if at least one visible piece comes off; dust alone is a miss. A No Bird does not count and is thrown again.

body.html: In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting each target has only two results: 'one' (a hit) or 'zero' (a miss). There are no half points.

A target is scored 'one' when three things are true. It was thrown correctly, the shooter fired as the rules require, and at least one visible piece broke off it (a target that shatters completely counts too). The same rule applies to flash targets (clays that release a puff of coloured powder when hit). A target is 'zero' (lost) when no visible piece comes off and there is only dust or smoke.
So the whole rule comes down to one thing you can see: a piece breaking off. A small chip that flies off counts as a hit. A puff of dust, with the target flying on in one piece, is lost.
Only the referee decides whether a target was hit. Squad members may not give opinions, and nobody may pick up a target to check it.

html.sporting: Break your targets where the referee can see the break. If a target breaks behind an obstacle or beyond the shooting limit (the edge of the area in which a break counts), the referee decides. That decision cannot be appealed. Once you call for the next target, you have accepted the decision on the last one.
html.compak: The referee announces each zero aloud or with a sound signal. Object at once, before the next shooter calls.

body.html: A No Bird is a target that does not count and is thrown again. The referee calls it when the target is thrown broken, comes from the wrong trap, or has the wrong colour (in Sporting™ also the wrong size or type). Other reasons are an irregular trajectory, a release more than 3 seconds late (see The call, time limits and lateness) or a target you did not call for. A No Bird is also given when something clearly disturbed you, or when the referee cannot judge the result.

html.sporting: Two targets leaving the traps of the same stand at once is also a No Bird.
html.compak: Bad weather does not give a No Bird, whatever the conditions. A target or pieces flying over from the neighbouring Compak® Sporting layout (the field next to yours) do not give one either. A stray target from a trap of your own layout does.

body.html: After a No Bird, a single target is simply thrown again. In a double it depends on which target was irregular: see Doubles: how they are shot and scored.
Once the referee has called No Bird, you may not shoot at that target. After a first warning, doing so is penalised in both disciplines; how the targets are then scored is in the rules guide.

html.sporting: For a sudden heavy shower or violent storm that looks short, the referee may stop shooting. If it lasts longer, the referee informs the jury.
html.compak: Only the Head Referee may stop shooting for a sudden downpour or storm. If it may last, the jury is informed.

body.html: If you think a call was wrong, raise your hand and say so before the next call. Arguing later does not change the score; how a protest works is in Results, protests and appeals.

notes.html: Coach slang can mean the opposite of the rules. 'Smoked it' praises a very clean break, while in the rules 'only dust or smoke' is a lost target. More in False friends on the shooting ground.
Also: 'dead' means a hit, and 'lost' means a miss; do not translate them word for word.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Dead — only a chip, but it counts.
phrases.meaning: A small visible piece broke off, so it is a hit.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Lost — you were just behind it.
phrases.meaning: A miss; the shot went behind the target.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Don't argue with me later — say it now, before you call.
phrases.meaning: An objection must be made at once; calling the next target accepts the ruling.

key_points.html: 'One': at least one visible piece broke off the target, or it shattered completely.
'Zero': no visible piece, only dust or smoke.
Only the referee decides; nobody picks up a target to check it; object at once.
A No Bird does not count and is thrown again; you may not shoot at a declared No Bird.
Compak® Sporting: bad weather does not give a No Bird.

did_you_know.html: On Compak® Sporting score sheets a hit is marked X and a miss O.

quiz.q: After the shot the target only gives off dust, and no piece is seen. What is the result?
quiz.explain: A hit needs at least one visible piece; dust or smoke alone is a zero.

quiz.q: Who decides whether a target was hit?
quiz.explain: The referee decides alone and may ask others for advice only on his or her own initiative.

quiz.q: In Compak® Sporting heavy rain starts, and you miss. What is the result?

options.text: A No Bird, if you ask

quiz.explain: In Compak® Sporting a broken target is 'one' and a miss is 'zero' in any weather. Only the Head Referee may stop shooting for a sudden storm.
